problem_statement: frivizn/news-website-template (Meridian Wire) is a hand-built static international-news template: a bold red-and-black masthead with a Home/World/Politics/Business/Sport/Entertainment navigation bar, a home page (index.html) built from real category story sections (World, Politics, Business, Sport, Entertainment — each a <section> with an <h2> and several <div class="story"> cards), and a dedicated World article page (article.html) with the lead report, a two-column article-plus-sidebar layout, a comment thread and a comment form. The home page needs its own native reader tool: a "Browse the desk" category filter placed directly above the story grid. Build it and finish it properly: (1) render a filter control row of chips (All / World / Politics / Business / Sport / Entertainment matching the real desks) plus a live readout, and wire it end to end so clicking a chip shows only that desk's real story cards and updates the readout to "Showing N of 19 stories · <Category>" (clicking World -> "Showing 3 of 19 stories · World"); "All" restores every desk. (2) Make the filter genuinely responsive so the chip row wraps and shares the width on a 390px phone (NOT by merely clipping the spill with overflow-x:hidden while the row still refuses to wrap), while keeping it a clean single row on desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) and preserving the Meridian Wire red-accent editorial look. (3) Carry the same "Browse the desk" title cross-page: place a compact desk strip on the World article page too (a small "Browse the desk" strip that links back to the home desks), so the feature is reachable from any page, not only the home page. Preserve the home hero, top stories, all category grids, and the article's headline, byline, body, images, sidebar, comments and navigation; this is a targeted native-feature build and responsive repair, not a redesign.
required_content: The home page carries a "Browse the desk" category filter directly above the story grid, with a chip row (All / World / Politics / Business / Sport / Entertainment) and a live readout, styled in the Meridian Wire red-accent / white editorial look — not an off-palette or collapsed treatment.

The filter is wired end to end: clicking a category chip shows only that desk's real .story cards (hiding the other category sections) and updates the '.deskfilter__readout' to reflect the selection (e.g. clicking World yields 'Showing 3 of 19 stories · World'), in addition to highlighting the active chip — the post-click terminal state must reflect the chosen desk, not the default full-count sentence. 'All' restores all 19 stories.

The home page shows NO horizontal overflow on a 390px mobile viewport: the chip row reflows (wraps / shares the width) so the document width matches the viewport within a small tolerance, rather than being clipped or hidden while a fixed non-wrapping row still forces the document wider than the screen.

The same "Browse the desk" title marker appears on BOTH the home page and the World article page (a compact desk strip on the article that links back to the home desks), so the feature is reachable cross-page, not only on the home page.
On desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) the filter renders as an intact single chip row and neither the home page nor the article page overflows horizontally.

The home hero, top stories and every category story grid, plus the article headline, byline, body paragraphs, figures, sidebar, comment thread, comment form, navigation and footer, remain intact across all viewports.
design_constraints: Preserve Meridian Wire's editorial identity: the red (#bb1919) accent, black-on-white type, Exo 2 headings and Open Sans body, the masthead and category navigation, and the two-column article/sidebar layout.
Fix the responsiveness of the filter's own chip row rather than clamping the whole page or applying a page-level overflow-x:hidden that would merely mask the symptom.

Style the filter and its cross-page desk strip to match the reference red/white editorial look; the rendered filter and the real story grid beneath it must be visually faithful to the reference, not a cramped or off-palette treatment that crushes the cards into an illegible pile.
The category chips must remain readable and keep their labels after the row reflows on mobile; do not drop or truncate chips to make the row fit.
Keep the filter's live readout in sync with the selected chip on every viewport so the control is trustworthy on a phone.
Do not alter the article's textual content, imagery, sidebar entries, comments or chrome, nor the home page story content, while building the feature and repair.
state_constraints: desktop_home / tablet_home / mobile_home capture the Meridian Wire home page (masthead, category navigation, hero, the 'Browse the desk' filter and the story grids) with no horizontal overflow on any viewport.

mobile_home / mobile_deskfilter capture the home page at 390px; in the defective baseline the fixed 720px non-wrapping chip row forces the document about 340px wider than the viewport, and the shallow bad fix (narrower 540px row plus overflow-x:hidden that still refuses to wrap) still overflows about 170px. The repaired reference reflows the row to 0px overflow.

desktop_deskfilter / mobile_deskfilter scroll the 'Browse the desk' filter into view over the real story grid: it must be visually faithful to the reference red-accent filter + legible story cards (the D3 visual states, which are also the D4 control surface).

desktop_deskfilter_world / desktop_deskfilter_politics / mobile_deskfilter_world click a category chip; the '.deskfilter__readout' must update to reflect the selection, e.g. 'Showing 3 of 19 stories · World' (the D4 interaction states).

desktop_article / tablet_article / mobile_article capture the World article; the same 'Browse the desk' title must be present as a compact cross-page desk strip (the D2 cross-page invariant, shared with the home filter title).
desktop_home_footer / desktop_article_footer / mobile_article_footer scroll to the footer and desktop_article_comments captures the article comment thread + sidebar (regression / asset states).

Source inspection confirms the template is served as static HTML/CSS/JS with no build step, that the filter markup lives in index.html (and the compact strip in article.html) and is styled by css/deskfilter.css, the filter behaviour lives in js/deskfilter.js, and that no page-level overflow-x:hidden clip is present to hide the symptom.

change_completion: The home page carries the 'Browse the desk' category filter over the real story grid and the chip click filters the real story cards while updating the '.deskfilter__readout' to reflect the selected desk.
The home page no longer overflows horizontally on a 390px mobile viewport and the 'Browse the desk' title is present cross-page on both the home and the article pages.
design_consistency: The filter and its cross-page desk strip keep the Meridian Wire red-accent editorial look (red chip outlines, black-on-white type) and match the reference rendering, with the real story cards beneath rendering legibly.
On desktop and tablet the chip row still reads as a single intact horizontal row.
regression: The static index.html and article.html continue to serve without a custom dev server.
The home hero, top stories, category grids and the article headline, body copy, images, sidebar, comments, navigation and footer remain intact and reachable.
responsive: 390px home page has no horizontal overflow and the filter chips wrap cleanly.
Desktop and tablet home and article pages remain overflow-free across all viewports.

author_notes: L4 rebuilt Repair/native-feature build on the Meridian Wire news-website-template. The graded lever is the home page's OWN 'Browse the desk' category filter over the real story grid (not a bolted-on widget). The bad control fails FOUR orthogonal gates: D6 no_horizontal_overflow (the narrowed 540px non-wrapping chip row plus overflow-x:hidden still leaves the mobile home page about 170px wider than the 390px viewport; the defective baseline overflows about 340px; reference reflows to 0), D3 visual_regression (the near-black slab under the desk region with the real chips and .story cards / headlines crushed together by big negative margins into a colliding illegible ghost heap fails pixelmatch/ssim/block_fidelity against the reference red-accent filter+grid on both desktop_deskfilter and mobile_deskfilter while the chip/card text still passes), D2 dom_assertions (the 'Browse the desk' title is added on the home page only, so the cross-page invariant fails on the article), and D4 interaction_assertions (clicking the World chip toggles .active and hides cards — the click trajectory succeeds so action_history passes — but never re-syncs the '.deskfilter__readout', so the post-interaction terminal state stays the default 'Showing 19 of 19 stories · All desks'). The defective baseline fails D6/D3/D2 but PASSES D4 (its filter is correctly wired), keeping D4 leg-orthogonal to the layout levers. Reference passes all gates with 0 console errors / 0 network failures across every state. Only css/deskfilter.css, js/deskfilter.js and the article compact-strip block differ across legs; the story data-category tagging and all page copy elsewhere are identical infrastructure across legs.
